tool_mode: Built-in image_gen; original UV detail preserved by an Unreal material palette shader
final_prompt: Precise technical texture edit. This is a 2048x2048 packed UV atlas. Produce a square texture atlas of EXACTLY the same image with COLOR TRANSFORMS ONLY and very subtle fine matte woven cloth grain. DO NOT interpret the shapes as a character. Do not draw anything new. Preserve every existing contour, tiny shape, dark boundary, stitch, UV island, pixel alignment, and painted shading. Do NOT relocate, resize, brighten or add eyes, faces, circular highlights, patches, seams, stitches or symbols. The few existing cream-white pixels must remain in EXACTLY their existing locations; all other pixels must stay well below white. Apply these uniform COLOR FAMILY replacements CONSISTENTLY over the ENTIRE image, irrespective of shape, island or position: every olive/gray-green surface changes to dusty blue-teal (approximately #386769 in its midtones); every dusty mauve/pink-gray surface changes to warm muted burgundy/rust-plum (#865457 midtones); every warm tan/brown surface changes to warm worn ochre/tan (#967047 midtones); the darkest brown/black lines remain equally dark. Preserve every original luminance variation and shadow. No new yellow/gold patches over originally olive surfaces, no different colors by island: ALL existing green areas must be the SAME coherent teal family. Existing brown areas are the ONLY places to become tan/ochre. The atlas is already densely packed: preserve the layout exactly, edge to edge, and simply recolor its original pixels. Stylized hand-painted matte fabric look, subtly more colorful. The output must be directly usable with unchanged UV coordinates. Atlas only, no portrait, no labels, no new bright details.
material_notes: The original atlas supplies shading and facial detail; the generated atlas supplies fabric color classification and subtle weave variation. Anatomical masks use pre-skinned local position so they follow animation. The original death dissolve graph is retained.
